run.question: Database connection timeouts are occurring for blue-whale app in namespace app-94

report.summary: The blue-whale workload itself is up: Deployment app-94/blue-whale (created 2026-11-20T21:24:39Z, generation 1) runs one pod, blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-fv8r2, which is Running/Ready with 0 restarts and only Normal events. Its container is configured with DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20. In namespace app-94 the Service named postgres selects app=postgres-db, and its Endpoints object has no subsets at all, while the only pod in app-94 is blue-whale — i.e. the database host name the app was given resolves to a Service with no backing pod. The only Postgres server observed in the cluster is Deployment postgres in namespace d-c6 (selector app=postgres, Service postgres.d-c6 with endpoint 10.244.0.30:5432, log 'database system is ready to accept connections' at 21:19:05Z), which is a different entity from the app-94 Service and is not what DB_HOST names. This makes the app-94 postgres Service (selector app=postgres-db with no matching pods and no endpoints) the single object where the fault most plausibly originates, but the conclusion is partial: the container produced zero log lines in the sampled window, the app code lives in a Secret that cannot be read, and Prometheus and Jaeger returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for every query in this Run, so blue-whale's own timeout/exception text, error rate and spans were not observed, and I cannot verify whether an app-94 database workload ever existed.

claims.text: Pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-fv8r2 in namespace app-94 is Running and Ready on node opspilot-m1-control-plane, started 2026-11-20T21:24:39Z, with 0 restarts.

Deployment app-94/blue-whale (created 2026-11-20T21:24:39Z, generation 1, deployment.kubernetes.io/revision 1, 1/1 ready) runs container blue-whale with image python:3.9-slim, command [python /app/app.py], env DB_HOST=postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local, DB_PORT=5432, DB_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT=30, DB_POOL_SIZE=20, and mounts a Secret volume named app-code at /app.

Service postgres in namespace app-94 (created 2026-11-20T21:24:39Z, ClusterIP 10.96.93.40, port 5432) has selector {app: postgres-db}; its last-applied configuration also records selector app=postgres-db.
The Endpoints object for Service app-94/postgres has no subsets (empty endpoint list), whereas Endpoints app-94/blue-whale resolves to 10.244.0.38:8080 pointing at pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-fv8r2.
At query time the only pod in namespace app-94 is blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-fv8r2 (image python:3.9-slim, 0 restarts); no postgres/database pod exists in app-94.
Across all namespaces the only Deployment named postgres is in namespace d-c6 (1/1 ready, selector app=postgres); there is no Deployment named postgres or postgres-db in namespace app-94.

In namespace d-c6, Service postgres selects app=postgres and has endpoint 10.244.0.30:5432 on pod postgres-5855b548b5-bv5ml; that pod's log shows PostgreSQL 17.2 listening on 0.0.0.0:5432 and 'database system is ready to accept connections' at 2026-11-20T21:19:05Z, plus an ERROR at 21:20:34Z 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction' for an INSERT INTO orders statement.

The only events recorded for namespace app-94 in the authorized window are Normal events at 2026-11-20T21:24:39-21:24:40Z: Deployment blue-whale 'Scaled up replica set blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 from 0 to 1', ReplicaSet blue-whale-6bdbd444c5 SuccessfulCreate, and Pod Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started for blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-fv8r2.

Cluster-wide events in the authorized window (42 items, 5 dropped as outside the window) group only under reasons ScalingReplicaSet, SuccessfulCreate, Scheduled, Pulled, Created and Started: 6 for app-94 (blue-whale) and 36 for a rollout of the d-c6 database deployments at 2026-11-20T21:19:02-21:19:03Z; no Warning-reason event appears in that grouping.

The reported database connection timeouts are explained by Service app-94/postgres having selector app=postgres-db with no matching pod in app-94 and therefore no endpoints, so the host name postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 that Deployment blue-whale is configured with points at a Service with no backing database.

A second candidate for the same symptom: the DB_HOST value on Deployment blue-whale points into app-94 where no database workload was deployed, while the only running Postgres server in the cluster is Deployment postgres in namespace d-c6 (Service postgres.d-c6, endpoint 10.244.0.30:5432); if that d-c6 instance is the intended database, the host reference (or a Service in app-94 that forwards there) is the misconfiguration. The app code that would reveal the intended target is in the unreadable Secret volume app-code, so this remains unverified.

The blue-whale pod shows no Kubernetes-level failure: phase Running, all conditions True (Initialized, Ready, ContainersReady, PodScheduled), containerStatuses ready=true with restartCount 0 and empty lastState (no terminated/OOMKilled state), and no Warning events in the window — so pod status alone does not show the app failing.

Rejected as the mechanism: that blue-whale's failures come from a crashing, OOMKilled or evicted pod. Restart count is 0, lastState is empty, the pod is Ready, and no Evicted/OOMKilled/BackOff/Failed/Unhealthy event exists in the sampled window.

Rejected as the cause of blue-whale's timeouts: the PostgreSQL ERROR 'cannot execute INSERT in a read-only transaction' at 2026-11-20T21:20:34Z. It was written by pod postgres-5855b548b5-bv5ml in namespace d-c6, a different entity from Service app-94/postgres that blue-whale's DB_HOST names, and no evidence links a blue-whale call to that server.

Check connectivity and the exact error from inside the blue-whale pod (for example resolving postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local and attempting a TCP connect / psql to port 5432) — this Run had no exec or equivalent probe tool, so that step of the database runbook could not be carried out.

Make the endpoint and the intended database agree: either deploy a Postgres workload in namespace app-94 carrying the label the Service selects (app=postgres-db) or correct Service app-94/postgres's selector to the labels the database actually has, and if the intended database is the d-c6 instance, point DB_HOST at that Service (postgres.d-c6.svc.cluster.local) rather than at an app-94 Service with no backing pod.

gaps: blue-whale's own application logs are missing: fetch_pod_logs for pod blue-whale-6bdbd444c5-fv8r2 (namespace app-94, window 2026-11-20T20:25:18Z-21:25:18Z, limit 200, with and without the error/timeout/connect/postgres/fail filter) returned status no_data with 0 lines read from the current container and no previous container instance, so the app's timeout or exception text was not observed; this shows only that no lines were returned, not that none were written.

Prometheus was unavailable for the whole Run: get_label_values, get_metric_names, get_metric_metadata, metrics_range_query and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (7 attempts between 21:25:37Z and 21:26:26Z), so no error-rate, latency, restart or endpoint-count series (e.g. kube_deployment_status_replicas_available{namespace="app-94"}, kube_pod_owner, traces_span_metrics_calls_total) could be read and no baseline could be established.

Jaeger was unavailable: traces_list_services and traces_search (including frontend and checkout) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, error-status or call-edge evidence for blue-whale or its database dependency exists in this Run; blue-whale also does not appear in the advertised available-service list, so its traces are unknown rather than absent.

Secrets cannot be read: Deployment blue-whale mounts Secret volume app-code at /app (the app.py the container runs) and possibly database credentials; the intended DB host, retry/timeout behaviour and any credential mismatch could not be verified.

Whether a database workload ever existed in namespace app-94 (or whether Service postgres's selector app=postgres-db ever matched a pod) is unknown: Kubernetes objects show only current state, and the change_history integration is not available in this Run.

NetworkPolicies, Ingresses and ResourceQuotas queries across the cluster returned no items (status no_data), which is not proof of absence: a policy or quota blocking or throttling the path from blue-whale to port 5432 remains unchecked.
A label-selector query for pods with app=postgres-db returned no items (status no_data), which likewise only shows that this query matched nothing at query time.

All Kubernetes object observations were taken around 2026-11-20T21:25:21Z-21:26:03Z, after the authorized window end (21:25:18Z); they describe current state and cannot prove the state during earlier parts of the window.
next_steps: Run an in-pod connectivity test from blue-whale to postgres.app-94.svc.cluster.local:5432 (DNS resolution, TCP connect, driver-level error) and capture the exact exception text, since no exec tool was available here.

Decide the intended database for blue-whale (an app-94 database or the d-c6 postgres Deployment) and reconcile Deployment env DB_HOST, Service app-94/postgres's selector and the actual Pod labels in one change.
Inspect the Secret app-code to confirm the application's actual DB host/port/retry behaviour and whether it authenticates against the intended server.
Re-establish Prometheus and Jaeger access and re-check blue-whale's error rate, latency and spans plus kube-state-metrics history of Service app-94/postgres endpoints before and during the window.
